title: fix(objectql): keep the metadata service's copy of a runtime-authored object current after boot (MCP stdio exposure gate)
body:
Fixes #23661

Clause-②: no

**reachable: true.** On a kernel whose `ObjectQLPlugin` has no `environmentId`, the MCP stdio door SERVED, read and write, an object whose API exposure had been switched off after boot, and kept listing and describing a deleted one. The producer is `packages/objectql`'s boot bridge: it copies each registry object into the `metadata` service once, and no authoring door wrote to that service afterwards. This PR keeps that copy current where it is produced. The MCP package is untouched, and so is `metadata-protocol` (the claim's stop condition on `protocol.ts` never came up).

## Step 1: the walk, on base `8d1fb1fb2d` (which carries #23659)

**How.** A real `ObjectKernel` with `MetadataPlugin` (a `NodeMetadataManager`, `watch: false`) and `ObjectQLPlugin` with no `environmentId`, over an in-memory driver. The MCP side is the real `MCPServerPlugin`: its `start()` builds the stdio data bridge (`createStdioDataBridge`, the code under `enforceApiExposure`), and the session is its own server on a real `StdioServerTransport` over `PassThrough` pipes, JSON-RPC `tools/call`. A test process cannot hand over its stdin, which is why the pipes. The one faked seam is the `sys_api_key` row the stdio principal resolves from (the engine is wrapped so that table answers one non-revoked key); the metadata service, the engine, the registry and the protocol are the kernel's own. The runtime object is `qa_probe_gadget`, saved exposed, two records, then a second boot so it is hydrated and bridged.

**(a) Exposure turned off after boot** (`saveMetaItem` with `enable.apiEnabled: false`, the door Studio uses):

```
registry.getObject(name).enable            {"apiEnabled":false}
metadata.getObject(name)  (label, enable)  "Gadget"  {"apiEnabled":true}
protocol getMetaItem(...).enable           {"apiEnabled":false}
query_records   isError false   {"object":"qa_probe_gadget","records":[{"name":"rec-1",...},{"name":"rec-2",...}],"total":2}
get_record      isError true    Record "nope" not found in "qa_probe_gadget"      (the exposure gate passed; the engine answered)
create_record   isError false   {"object":"qa_probe_gadget","id":"r_38008a8c-...","record":{"name":"leak-probe",...,"created_by":"usr_stdio","updated_by":"usr_stdio",...}}
rows in the table afterwards    3   (it held 2)
describe_object isError false   {"name":"qa_probe_gadget","label":"Gadget","fields":[...8 fields...],"enableFeatures":{"apiEnabled":true}}
```

**(b) Deleted** (`deleteMetaItem` answered `{"success":true,"reset":true}`):

```
registry.getObject(name)                   absent
metadata.getObject(name)                   still answers
list_objects                               still names qa_probe_gadget
describe_object isError false              {"name":"qa_probe_gadget","label":"Gadget","fields":[...],"enableFeatures":{"apiEnabled":true}}
query_records   isError true               {"error":{"code":"OBJECT_NOT_FOUND","message":"Object 'qa_probe_gadget' not found","status":404}}
```

**(c) A runtime object created after boot, `apiEnabled: false` from the first save.** Nothing in the card measured this, and it is the widest of the three: such an object has no copy at all.

```
registry.getObject(name).enable            {"apiEnabled":false}
metadata.getObject(name)                   undefined   (ABSENT)
query_records                              SERVED
list_objects names it                      false
refuseUnexposedDataAction (the runtime dispatcher's gate; callData, under the HTTP MCP data verbs, asks it first)
                                           ALLOWED
```

**(d) A code package's object cannot change after boot.** The same save is refused: `Metadata item 'object/qa_shipped_widget' is provided by a managed package and is sealed against in-place edits: its type takes no environment overlay (allowEnvironmentOverlay=false)...`. So the only copies that can go stale are runtime-authored ones, which bounds this fix.

The elisions above are generated ids, timestamps and the platform fields `describe_object` lists; every verdict, code and count is as the door answered. The HTTP MCP door itself was not walked; (c) measures the gate function it calls, handed this kernel's `metadata` service.

## Landing point, measured, and what "fails closed" means here

`enforceApiExposure` does not fail closed on a missing or unreadable definition. It falls open by design, the same decision the HTTP gate makes (pinned by `stdio-data-bridge.exposure.test.ts`: "falls open when the metadata read throws", "falls open when the object does not resolve"). Reading (c) is that rule at work: an ABSENT copy served an `apiEnabled: false` object. So the landing point has to be the one that never leaves a live object's definition stale or absent, and that is absent only when the registry no longer has the object, where the engine refuses it. Measured:

| landing | turned off after boot | created after boot, off | deleted |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| none (base) | SERVED | SERVED (no copy, gate falls open) | listed and described; data verbs refused by the engine |
| copy refreshed in place, removed on delete (this PR) | REFUSED `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` 404 | REFUSED | not listed; describe: not found; data verbs `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` 404 |

A landing that DROPS the copy on save instead of refreshing it is not built: reading (c) is what it would produce, because absent reads as no declaration.

**Why the producer and not the door.** The same copy is read by the runtime dispatcher's exposure gate (measured ALLOWED in (c), now REFUSED), by the AI tools and by the MCP resources; making the stdio door read the registry would have fixed one of those readers, would have needed `engine.registry`, which `IDataEngine` does not declare, in four places of `packages/mcp` (the bridge's gate, list and describe, the `get_record` resource reader in `plugin.ts`, the resources), and would have left the rest stale. The seam is the one every authoring door already emits, `onMetadataMutation`; it also replays on a cluster peer once the peer's registry has converged, which a door change would not cover. `plugin-security`'s security-catalog echo already mirrors stored rows into this service the same way.

## What changed

- `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`: the existing `onMetadataMutation` subscription calls the new `followRuntimeObjectCopy` for `object` events. Four hunks (the import, the subscription, a docblock note on the bridge, the new methods after it); the start-order region (#23649) is not touched.
  - A save refreshes the copy before it returns, through `registerInMemory` (synchronous, no persistence, no announce). A service without it gets the bridge's own `register(..., { notify: false })`.
  - A delete removes the copy only when the mutation says `deleted`, the registry no longer serves the name, and the copy is the runtime-authored one (`_provenance: 'org'`). The removal is `unregister`, the service's one removal, which also deletes through writable `datasource:` loaders; the three conditions are what bound that, as in the security-catalog echo. The registry is asked again afterwards: a re-creation that landed while the removal awaited its loaders has its copy put back.
  - A code package's copy is never touched: the follow acts when the registry's owner row for the name is tenant-authored, or the copy already is.
  - A refresh that fails is logged at `error`, with the consequence and the way out.
  - Armed on the shape the bridge runs on (no `environmentId`).
- `packages/objectql/src/plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts` (new) and `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mcp-stdio-runtime-object-exposure.test.ts` (new): the pins.
- `.changeset/23661-runtime-object-metadata-copy.md`: patch for `@objectstack/objectql`.

## Pins, and the ablation

Producer pins (real kernel, the service's answers), `plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts`: toggled off after boot (the copy says so before the save returns, and the listing agrees); created after boot (a copy at once); deleted (copy and listing entry gone, a code package's copy the very entry the bridge wrote); deleted then created again while the removal is held at `unregister` (the new object keeps its copy); and a CONTROL (a code package's copy untouched by runtime edits and by a delete naming its own object; a runtime object that stays exposed keeps saying so).

Door pins (real kernel, real `MCPServerPlugin`, an in-process JSON-RPC transport), `mcp-stdio-runtime-object-exposure.test.ts`: CONTROL (an exposed runtime object is listed, described, queried and written through the door); toggled off after boot (`query_records`, `get_record`, `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record` refused with `OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / 404, the table untouched, the exposed neighbour still served); created after boot with exposure off (refused from the first call); deleted (not listed, describe says not found, data verbs `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`, the neighbour still listed).

Ablations, each leg with the mutation proved on disk by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit once, blob changed) and the restore proved (`blob == HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty):

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| objectql 1 | the `onMetadataMutation` call to `followRuntimeObjectCopy` deleted | 4 failed, 1 passed (the CONTROL stays green by design) |
| objectql 2 | the re-judge after `unregister` deleted | 1 failed (the re-creation pin), 4 passed |
| door, base dist | `@objectstack/objectql` dist built from base, before the fix | 3 failed, 1 passed (CONTROL) |
| door, mutant dist | the subscription's type test spelled so it never fires, objectql rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 2 built files | 3 failed, 1 passed (CONTROL) |
| door, restored | source restored, objectql rebuilt, marker absent from all 14 built files | 4 passed |

The first door ablation (the call deleted) did not complete its rebuild, so its reading is void and was redone with the compile-safe mutation above. The objectql pins import `plugin.ts` by source, so their legs need no rebuild.

## Verification (readings at `da8d0047c4` unless marked; every locked run printed `VERDICT command-exit 0`)

**Patch round, head `e55180423b`.** The one change is the deletion of an unused `const SYSTEM` in `plugin-runtime-object-metadata-copy.test.ts`. It was TS6133 under `noUnusedLocals`, and it made `TypeScript Type Check` red at `da8d0047c4` (contract record 6195385587). The fix was reproduced red and then green at the new head: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK, ledger unchanged at 39 files, 233 errors, 64 pins), and the 5 objectql pins pass. `plugin.ts` is byte-identical across the heads.


- Closure builds, then a full `turbo run build` (75 tasks, 74 cache hits, 0 failed).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: this reading was taken at `0ae4226d8b`, before the new test file existed, so it did not cover `da8d0047c4`. That head was red (see the patch round above), and the reading at `e55180423b` replaces it.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local`: 424 files, 8128 tests passed (this PR adds one file and five pins to the 423 files and 8123 tests the #23659 report measured).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck`: exit 0. Dogfood, the new pin plus seven real-stack files that author objects at runtime (`object-designer-field-reorder`, `picklist-shared-across-objects`, `package-first-authoring`, `managed-content-sealed`, `meta-published-and-state-routes`, `multi-package-artifact`, `external-validate-sees-runtime-save`): 8 files, 49 tests passed. `metadata-protocol` (3 files, 263 tests) and `service-automation` (6 files, 52 tests), the suites that author through the protocol on a real `ObjectQLPlugin`: passed. The full dogfood gate is CI's.
- `eslint . --no-inline-config` over the whole tree: 9179 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 68 families, plus the 52 artifact-roster families and the 11 declared wide-population families, 130 commands: 130 commands run at `da8d0047c4`, each exit code captured before any pipe: 126 exited 0. That includes all 68 derived families (the `--ran` reconciliation: 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, exit 0), the roster and wide families that need no pull request, and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which exited 3 on a first run for want of a `dist/` and exited 0 after the full build. Four exited non-zero because they need a pull request or a workflow event a local run does not have, and are NOT MEASURED here (CI runs them): `check-closing-target-claim` (2), `check-single-claim-paths` (2), `check-governed-queue-guard` (1), and `check-partof-closing-keyword` (2), which exits 0 when handed this body in `PR_BODY`. This diff touches no governed surface.

## Acceptance notes

- **The gate still falls open on a missing definition.** Not changed here: it is the HTTP gate's decision too, and the engine refuses an object it does not hold (reading (b)). Whether either gate should refuse a missing definition is a separate decision, and an unreadable service still reads as open.
- **A kernel with an `environmentId` is unchanged.** It does not run the boot bridge and its service is sourced from the artifact. Whether a runtime-authored object has a copy there, and so whether the stdio gate sees its exposure, was NOT MEASURED.
- **A cluster peer** converges its registry and then replays the mutation to local listeners, which is the seam used; no two-node run was made. NOT MEASURED.
- **The removal is not instantaneous.** A save is done before it returns; a delete's removal awaits the service (microtasks, plus a loader read if one is attached), so the listing drops the name a moment after the delete answers. The data verbs of a deleted object are refused by the engine from the delete on. The pins wait for it.
- **Package uninstall** deletes its rows through `deleteMetaItem`, so runtime-authored copies follow; the copies of a code package's own objects are not removed by this change or by the late-manifest bridge. NOT MEASURED.
